title: Two-Phase Decommit Protocol & Entrance Gating for Cycle Runways
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Mid-cycle scope erosion and surprise over-commits cause repeated mid-sprint decommits that derail velocity. We need an operational playbook that reduces churn and preserves delivery predictability without blocking high-value work.

Proposal summary: Create a two-phase decommit protocol plus an "entrance gating" system for incoming requests/features. Key concepts:
- Entrance gating: Every candidate feature must be labeled Gate A (ready for full commit), Gate B (buffer candidate), or Gate C (backlog). Gate A entry requires defined owner, dependency map, test signal, and a lightweight OKR alignment note. Gate B is allowed into the cycle only as buffer capacity.
- Two-phase decommit: 1) Soft decommit window (T-7 to T-3 days before approx mid-cycle review) where owners are asked to confirm or downgrade from Gate A to Gate B with 72h notice; 2) Hard decommit at T-2 days where items downgraded to Gate B are removed and replaced from a pre-approved buffer list.
- On-call float pool: maintain a small float of engineers (2-4 FTE-equivalent depending on cycle size) who are cross-trained to absorb urgent reassignments or buffer promotions to avoid single-team blockers.

Metrics and heuristics:
- Value density score = (expected customer impact * OKR alignment weight) / estimated team-days. Use this to rank Gate A vs Gate B.
- Skill friction multiplier to demote items that require >2 teams or >3 cross-repo changes.
- Commitment churn rate target: <10% of items decommitted after hard decommit.

Rollout plan:
1) Draft playbook and acceptance criteria in Confluence; run tabletop with ENG leads and Design owners (1 week).
2) Pilot in Cycle 2025-W04 with two product teams and a floating on-call pool.
3) Instrument dashboard (commit list, value density, skill friction, decommit events) and provide weekly digest.
4) After pilot, adjust thresholds and codify in the cycle intake template.

Acceptance criteria:
- Entrance gating checklists available in cycle intake template and used by >80% of new items in pilot teams.
- Soft decommit reminders auto-sent and at least 90% of owners respond within 72h in pilot.
- Dashboard shows decommit rate <10% after hard decommit in pilot cycle.

Trade-offs and notes:
- This increases upfront process friction (additional gating) but reduces mid-cycle firefighting. We will keep Gate A checklist minimal to limit friction.
- On-call float introduces staffing overhead; pilot will use existing rotations where possible.

Next steps:
- Finalize playbook doc and circulate by 2025-01-17.
- Build dashboard ticket with ENG observability (linked).
- Schedule tabletop exercises with leads (target week 2025-01-20).
